payload.docs_match:
KILLER. Docs match the surface, checked in the direction that catches drift: reading each doc as an owner would FOLLOW it, not comparing it to the code I remembered writing.

se.guidance-phone-setup is the enablement home and now teaches three things: how to pair (unchanged, i8c's QR), WHEN A PUSH HAPPENS (new - your rule, in your words), and the optional brief store (new - it existed nowhere). Every claim was checked against the code: the JSON shape matches the loader's four required fields; 'confirmed servable before it is announced' matches publishBrief; 'expires with its offer, capped at 6h' matches the offer's own deadline; 'drops to the actions-only rung' matches the whitelist returning null.

The drift that mattered was in the VERIFY step: it told you to reach a gate and wait for a buzz - which, under the corrected rule, correctly never comes for a gate the agent self-blesses. Following your own doc would have had you waiting for nothing. Fixed.

se_wait's TOOL DESCRIPTION now says that waiting on an offer summons a paired phone. That is the doc an agent reads before any guidance, and leaving it silent would have been the most expensive omission of the sweep.
payload.packaged:
Versioned by the close itself: the tag iter/i8d-phone-brief is created BEFORE the merge, so the full record stays reachable at the tag while trunk receives only the live claims (the i5d split, shipped this morning).

Trunk receives: engine/brief.ts (new), engine/phone.ts (rewritten), the park seam in engine/wait.ts, the wiring in engine/tools.ts, bin/se-board.ts with its announce timer removed, tests/i8d-brief.test.ts (19 checks), and the ledger updates.

Configuration baselined by EXCLUSION, deliberately: phone.json and brief.json are machine-local, hold secrets, and are not in the package - the product works without them, silent and at the actions-only rung.

ZERO new runtime dependencies. Your one-click install is intact.

Entry script: RECORDED SKIP with its reason - this adds no binary and no process, and the remaining setup is a click plus an owner-only third-party account step that was ruled out of scope at M4.
payload.dependencies_ruled:
Zero runtime npm dependencies, unchanged - and held there on purpose. The crypto rides node:crypto plus the platform's Web Crypto (the same implementation the browser runs, so one codebase serves both ends); the store rides fetch.

One NEW external service: Cloudflare Workers KV as the brief host. Opt-in per machine, absent by default, and NOT load-bearing - without it you lose the third action and nothing else. The floor of the lane (summon, tap) depends on neither the store nor anything beyond ntfy.

kb is stamped ABSENT on all ten grants, which is the correct state after the junction incident.

No new ask is owed: the two decisions that would need you are already ruled - one-click install (nothing added, moot) and evidence content on a third-party host (your accepted-risk model, extended and tripwired).

Nothing upstream was patched or forked, so no proposal is deposited. Both external protocols behaved as specified; the failures were entirely ours.
payload.handover_accepted:
KILLER - and this one is yours, not mine.

WHAT THIS ITERATION FIXED, all three witnessed by you: (1) the bless button errored with 'Expected URL scheme HTTP or HTTPS but was answer' - action URLs are now absolute, built at send time, as v1 always did; (2) the rich encrypted brief the design document recorded as BUILT AND VERIFIED at §18 was never actually in v2 - it is now, proven live end to end against the real store in 687ms; (3) pushes fired from a board timer that could not know your intent - the push now happens exactly when the run PARKS, which is your rule: push when I would otherwise be waiting for you.

THE PROOF IS THIS ITERATION'S OWN CONDUCT: ten gates walked, nine self-blessed under your grant, and not one of them touched your phone. This one did.

WHAT I CANNOT PROVE, and the reason you are holding this: whether the card renders and the tap fires on YOUR device. No test substitutes for a thumb. That leg is D1, it was flagged UNVERIFIED in the design document, it shipped unverified in i8, and that is the whole reason i8d exists - so I will not self-bless it.

If you tapped BLESS from the phone, you have just proven the loop by using it to close the thing that built it, and the grant will record channel=phone, adjudicated_by=owner. If the card is wrong, the brief will not open, or the tap errors: dismiss it, tell me what you saw, and it does not ship.

One honest note: the battery is green and the chain is proven, but everything above rests on a device I have never seen.
